title: Instrument-dependent measurement of privacy leakage in retrieval-augmented generation: corpus, evaluation harness and analysis artifacts
description:
Reproducibility artifact for the study of privacy leakage in enterprise retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Contains the deterministic synthetic corpus generator and its entity-level annotations (155 documents, 2,190 annotations, seed 42), the 57-scenario adversarial registry across four attacker profiles and eight attack families, the evaluation engine implementing the binary leakage function L and severity score S, the LLM-judge harness and its versioned system prompts, per-execution logs for the undefended baseline and all six defense-ablation configurations, both human-labelled judge calibration samples, and every analysis script used to produce the reported statistics.

Synthetic data notice. The corpus is entirely synthetic (Faker, seed 42). It deliberately contains credential-shaped strings — API-key, JWT, database-connection-string, private-key and password-hash patterns — because detecting them is part of what the study measures. These are generated values, not live secrets. Automated secret scanners will flag them; that is expected and is why the artifact is deposited here rather than on a code-hosting platform with push protection.

No live credentials. No .env file, no API key and no git history are included. The archive was scanned against every real credential value known to the project and none is present.
